target_boundary: A product-view local HTML presentation about research/agentic-music-studio/Agentic-Music-Studio.pdf, reframed around problem, solution, insights, leverage, and a musician day-in-the-life.

reader_contract.target_public: A reader who wants to understand the product opportunity, not only the research note: musicians, tool builders, researchers, or product collaborators.
assumed_knowledge: The reader knows that software can render audio from code.
The reader can follow a left-to-right pipeline diagram.
The reader does not need prior knowledge of Xenakis, Sethares, TidalCycles, or NIME.
reader_contract.reader_reward: The reader can explain the customer problem, why the product exists, how the spec-centered solution works, what insights were learned, how others can leverage it, and what a musician's day with the studio feels like.

must_start_with: Start with the musician's problem: choosing between control and speed.
Make the product promise visible before introducing implementation details.
must_not_start_with: Do not start with a generic research summary.
Do not imply that a model generates audio.
Do not bury the reproducible spec behind decorative visuals.
opening_contract.failure_message: If the deck does not explain the product problem and product use, it fails the revised request.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: Musicians should be able to move fast from intent to sound without losing inspectable craft.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It frames the deck around the user problem rather than around implementation alone.
reader_terms.source_or_lane: Product framing inference from Agentic-Music-Studio.pdf and LEARNING-PACK.md; surface lane
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not treat the product bet as proven market demand; it is a presentation framing around the source proof.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A studio where the human gives intent and judgment while an agent performs deterministic engineering over inspectable code and specs.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It keeps the human in charge of taste while moving the engineering grind into a reproducible system.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not use the term to mean a model that directly generates sound.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: The shared, reproducible document that every interface edits and the engine can replay from a seed.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It is the craft-preserving artifact: diffable, inspectable, forkable, and replayable.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: A prompt alone is not the spec if it cannot reproduce the audio path.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A deterministic tuning loop that changes synth parameters to hit measured perceptual targets.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: The PDF says the intelligence lives in search against real measurements, not in black-box audio generation.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not treat the optimized metric as proof that a listener will feel the named emotion.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: The baseline feature measurements the studio trusts before optimizing or making claims.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: The PDF reports that peak-picking drifted 6.1 percent on GENDYN, while multitaper moment centroid drifted 1.3 percent.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not assume a feature is stable just because the code computes a number.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: Steering across trade-offs where improving one target can worsen another.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: The PDF shows that adding bite increases dissonance and centroid, trading away some darkness.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not present every critique as a simple improvement on all dimensions.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A measured stand-in for a felt effect, such as using dissonance as a stand-in for strangeness.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: The source explicitly keeps felt effect claims open until listener evidence exists.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not claim the proxy equals the listener's experience.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A kind of exchange between musician and studio, such as command, critique, annotation, performance, or feedback.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It lets other people leverage the work as a reusable product pattern, not only as one interface.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not collapse process into modality; voice can carry many different process types.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a newcomer, I want to know the product problem first.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Musicians should not have to choose between expressive control and fast exploration.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: framing the studio as a product opportunity rather than only a technical proof.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a working reader, I want the product motion in one glance.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Intent becomes a spec, the agent writes inspectable code, objective search tunes it, deterministic render creates audio, and critique loops back.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: seeing how the product turns a musician's words into editable sound.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a reviewer, I want to see which insights shape the product.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Closed measurable primitives support open objectives, stable measurements support search, and visible trade-offs support steering.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: understanding why the UI must expose measurements and trade-offs.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a builder, I want to know how other people can leverage the work.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: The pattern can support musicians, tool builders, researchers, live coders, educators, and product teams.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: making the deck useful beyond the original proof artifact.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As an implementer, I want the proof stage, day-in-life flow, and next gates.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: v1 proves the core loop while roadmap gates decide how broadly the product generalizes.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: connecting current proof to practical musician use.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a skeptical reader, I want product claims separated from proof.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: The problem framing and leverage categories are product inference; measured drift, working render, and no-model sound path are source-backed.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: keeping the product story useful without over-claiming evidence.

evidence: The PDF title is Agentic Music Studio.
The PDF says the human supplies intent and taste while the agent does deterministic engineering over one shared reproducible spec.
The PDF says no generative model touches the sound path.
The LEARNING-PACK frames the core idea as supplying intent and taste while the agent does deterministic engineering.
inference: The product-view deck should open with the musician's problem: control versus speed.

evidence: The source says the artifact is authored, diffable, replayable code, not a black-box output.
The source says a model may only parse intent into an inspectable spec.
The PDF says v1 renders playable audio from the operator's own example.
inference: The deck treats reproducibility, inspectability, seeded code, and no-model sound path as product trust properties.

evidence: The PDF names studio-core as the engine and measurement floor.
The PDF names intent-engine as the intent-to-agent-written-code-to-sound layer.
The research findings define ten communication processes, all editing one shared spec.
Definitions.md defines communication process as a speech-act plus initiative-profile.
inference: The presentation groups leverage audiences around reusable product patterns.

evidence: The PDF says effects are open objectives over a small closed set of measurable primitives.
The PDF says the floor must be measured, not assumed.
The PDF says steering is Pareto navigation because dark and strangeness conflict.
inference: The product insights slide translates these findings into interface requirements.

evidence: The PDF cites Xenakis dynamic stochastic synthesis, Sethares, Thomson multitaper spectral estimation, TidalCycles, and NIME.
The PDF says each key finding is backed by an artifact: a test, a measurement, or an adversarial review.
The README says the research tower is local-only and not a build spec.
inference: The deck frames musicians, builders, researchers, live coders, educators, and product teams as leverage audiences.

evidence: The PDF pipeline is INTENT -> SPEC -> PROGRAM -> RENDER -> STEER.
The pipeline example starts from dark violin stochastic and bring strangeness.
The source says human hears, reads/edits code, and critiques, then loops back.
inference: The deck adds a musician day-in-the-life path to make the pipeline feel like product use.

evidence: The PDF says v1 is a working proof and success.
The PDF names Spectralize-v2, O1 felt-match, Steering-v2, and scope expansion as deliberately open.
The PDF says the method used research towers, a tensioned multi-agent design dispatch, layered build plans, adversarial verification, and refresh cycles.
inference: The open-work slide orders follow-up as product validation gates rather than missing features.
Does a dissonance objective predict felt strangeness for listeners?
Can open-vocabulary intent be governed without vocabulary drift?
Can roughness become as analyzer-independent as darkness?
How should a human steer trade-offs beyond weighted-sum tuning?
Which leverage audiences are real adoption paths versus presentation hypotheses?
Does the day-in-life story match actual musician workflow?

evidence: The x-ray renderer ladder accepts L0 static HTML/SVG as the default proof path.
The x-ray library patterns used are lifecycle-stack, dependency-boundary, process-branch, and evidence-inference-split.
The x-ray validator requires source-backed and inference markers, reader terms, reader outcomes, and the L0 static HTML/SVG marker.
inference: A deck with keyboard/button navigation, source markers, inline SVG diagrams, and no remote dependencies fits the user's request for an HTML presentation.
